# Bounded tool-loop profile (`tool-loop-v1`)

This ten-case input-only profile compares the public bounded tool loop. Each case holds literal initial messages and ordered text parts, entry-point selector, target, round limit, explicit `tool_choice`, client context/catalog switches, route retry/health settings, ordered tool declarations and closed handler inputs, and a reference to its ordered provider response script. Initial messages are decoded to actual public `ai.Message`/`ai.Text` values; supported initial roles are system, user, and assistant. Tool-result roles belong to the loop-generated history, where their call IDs are preserved.

The corpus contains no expected outcomes, dispatch lists, or request bodies. The closed input grammar permits recursive JSON only for tool parameter schemas, tool-call arguments, and constant handler data. `observations.schema.json` is the paired trace grammar: it accepts only Python/C# runtime labels, requires ten records with the closed case-ID set, and requires request model, role-discriminated messages, advertised tools, and tool choice. The pure aggregate validator additionally requires the records to match corpus IDs exactly once and in order.

Focused controls execute all ten cases through the actual public async or sync `run_tools` APIs against the deterministic fake transport, construct and validate the complete actual-shaped aggregate, and test aggregate omissions, duplicates, unknown IDs, and reordering. The multi-message/multi-part case confirms every initial message and text part reaches the actual outgoing request. Git provenance (HEAD and porcelain dirty state) is read from the selected repository root; the test verifies `ai.__file__` remains under that checkout's `src/python` before capturing execution.

Case IDs, in order: `tools-final-no-calls`, `tools-one-call`, `tools-ordered-calls`, `tools-repeated-id`, `tools-duplicate-name`, `tools-round-exhaustion`, `tools-zero-rounds`, `tools-negative-rounds`, `tools-unknown-name`, `tools-sync-path`.

Comparison requires the same source revision, dirty state and literal corpus in both runtimes, with every record present exactly once in input order. Handler facts, outgoing request fields and final result values compare exactly. At the public error boundary, Python records its actual `ToolLoopError` and C# records its actual `ToolLoopException`; these two runtime-specific type names map directionally. Only the error message, detail and hint are free diagnostic text, including null where the runtime supplies none. They remain in the original observations and are excluded only at those exact public-error paths in the comparison copy. Nested handler data and request strings receive no such normalization.

This profile qualifies only the bounded tool-loop behavior described here. It does not establish full SDK parity, clean-source qualification or release readiness.
